Dear Council members, I recently was surveyed on a plan to develop new trails in Salt Lake City. I love the idea of new trails, but I think the money would be better spent at this time to take better care of the ones we already have. I no longer walk on the Jordan River Trail that is close to my neighborhood (I live in the Fair Park Neighborhood) because of the amount of garbage along the trail. My child and my dog love to go to Cottonwood Park, but I have seen used needles there, our car window got smashed there and things stolen, and we have seen people, apparently indigent, on the grass and felt like we needed to check if they were alive or not. Those things make it not so pleasant. I would suggest that in addition to hiring more people to pick up garbage, Salt Lake devotes whatever resources it has to expanding the amount of mental health and addiction beds and increasing enforcement of public drunkenness or drug use laws, squatting laws, and littering laws. I also think that urban camp sites should be set up with trash collection and sanitation with frequent police presence in some areas. All along the river at Cottonwood park are camps set up. Some are tidy and the inhabitants do not interfere with the intended uses of the areas; but some aren't. Making the existing recreational areas function better as recreational areas and not as homeless camps, and providing better options to unhoused people, should be a much higher priority than creating new trails. Sincerely, Camilla Flint

To whom it may concern, Over the course of the last year, I have been appalled at the handling of the riots and the treatment of our police department in Salt Lake City. During one of the riots, the rioters stopped my car, threw bottles at it at 500 south and state, flipped me off, danced in front of my car, cursed, all while the police were not allowed to do anything about it. I felt so sorry for them that I went and bought a bag of treats and sodas, hoping to apologize for the brutal abandonment by Mayor Mendenhall and all leadership. In my opinion, she, the city council, and the chief of police should be investigated for sedition for what they allowed to occur. The day after the destruction of the DA's office, once again I bought pizzas, made cupcakes, and wrote a thank you note to the officers and dropped it off at the police station; and then volunteered to clean the paint and broken glass left by the criminals who violated the building. I wonder how many times the leadership has done the same for these brave people or volunteered to clean up the mess that they themselves created? My own brother was killed by police last summer in another state, and I am biracial, and I do NOT support one bit the lashing that the police have received, and the mayor and leaders should be absolutely ashamed of what they allowed to occur. My race and circumstances of my family should not have any bearing in what is right and correct, but due to the political zeitgeist, I have to qualify my opinion now with those facts, otherwise I am not allowed a dog in the fight because I would not be perceived as having any right to speak my mind. The city leadership has let the mob of a minor few, who have mouths, tempers, and lack of restraint, to speak for us. STOP LISTENING TO THEM! Somehow the first amendment has become the newest gym for people; I have to exercise my 1st amendment right today; gotta get 20 more reps in before lunch. What would happen if people exercised other rights with the same vehemence that has run rampant with the 1st? What if people exercised their 2nd amendment right with the same unchecked restraint?! Why is it then any different for those who incite violence with their words; who damage our community; who let the homeless camps take over; who glorify criminals, who were caught breaking the law, with murals? What is wrong with the leadership who now redefine words, that racism is now included with a qualifier of not only being against another race, but against another race by those in authority? That is subjective at best. Where is the line where you can stop and say I guess we went too far now? The fact that the city painted a black lives matter mural proves their hypocrisy and idiocy. Instead of inspiring and encouraging us to be Americans first, and to only judge by the content of character, the mayor and her subordinates have systematically said and done, time and again, that they are racists by separating us. The mayor, and those who serve with her, have now created isolation and segregation through their hubris and perverse interpretation of diversification, so congratulations. Enough is enough. Dan White

I consider the city council and Mayor Mendenhall actions as the major reason why police are leaving and more importantly, why crime in Salt lake City is up 25% for the year. Your decisions to support anti-police groups are wise and irresponsible. If the crime and negative attitude towards police doesn?t change soon, I will be actively encouraging everyone I know in Salt Lake City to vote you all out.

I am a resident of washington county. I am writing to demand that the City Council adopt a budget for the people, that prioritizes community wellbeing and redirects funding away from the police. We are in the midst of widespread upheaval over the systemic violence of policing, embodied by the SLCPD's well documented history of lethal force against residents of color. Empty gestures and suggestions of ?reform are unacceptable. I am demanding the voices of this movement be heard, and that real change be made to the way this city allocates its resources. Support for marginalized communities is necessary now, more than ever. But instead, the Mayor has proposed an increase in funding to the SLCPD, while social services and education--proven to better promote community safety than policing--stagnate. The SLCPD has seen a rise in overtime pay which, when too often paid out to officers responsible for harassing unhoused, Black, Indigenous, and Latinx residents, is deeply insulting. I am demanding that the City Council defund the SLCPD. I demand a budget that adequately and effectively meets the needs of impacted Utahans during this trying and uncertain time, when livelihoods are on the line. I demand a budget that supports community wellbeing, rather than empowering the police forces that tear us apart. Although City Council has thus far avoided voting or revising Mayor Mendenhall's budget proposal, the document is back in your hands. It is your duty to represent your constituents. I am urging you to completely revise the SLC budget for 2020-2021 fiscal year, and to fund care, not criminalization and incarceration. You must adopt a budget for the people. Public opinion is with me. Thank you for your time, James Ream
